name: Kameron Battle
strengths: Battle presses the line, plants once, and is already gone — one-cut decisiveness with no dance in the hole.
Battle finds cutback daylight when outside zone over-pursues and finishes with a clear second gear that pulls away in the open field.
Battle keeps his feet through arm tackles and low-ankle grabs, falling forward with compact contact balance.
Battle catches the ball cleanly in stride on swing/check work and turns upfield without gearing down.
weaknesses: Battle still needs SEC mass on a ~5-9 / 180 frame — square hits from bigger LBs can stand him up before he can use elusiveness.
Battle runs a tick upright through interior creases at times and needs to sink pads more consistently into contact.
comparison: Battle comps to Justice Hill — 5-10 / ~190 mold; compact one-cut burst, cutback vision, and enough receiving juice to stay on the field (size-matched within ~1–2" of Battle's ~5-9 / 180 frame).
projection: Battle projects as a Year 1–2 package / big-play back who develops into the RB rotation, then competes for every-down snaps — ceiling as a compact SEC feature back who stresses defenses between the tackles and in space.
schemeFit: Battle fits a zone/gap RB room that wants one-cut vision, cutback feel, and pass-game versatility out of the backfield.
insiderNotes: Battle is a compact one-cut runner with cutback vision and a real second gear once he clears the second level. Presses the designed hole without dancing, keeps his feet through arm tackles, and shows natural hands on swing routes. Florida has ramped communication nonstop and already locked a game-day visit while sitting atop his On3 RPM board.
